title: Physical fitness changes following group-based interval small-sided games among middle school soccer players
venue: Interpersona An International Journal on Personal Relationships
abstract: Objective: This study examined changes in aerobic fitness, resting and exercise heart rates, and sprint performance following an eight-week interval-based small-sided games program among middle school students participating in extracurricular soccer. Methods: Twenty-four male students from SMP Negeri 6 Palu, Indonesia, participated in a one-group pretest–posttest study involving 24 training sessions. The intervention consisted of 4 vs. 4 small-sided games played on a 30 × 25 m pitch in four 4-min bouts, separated by 2 min of passive recovery. Aerobic fitness was assessed using the Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 1 and expressed as estimated maximal oxygen uptake (VO₂max). Heart rate was measured at rest and during exercise, while sprint performance was evaluated using a 30-m sprint test. Pretest and posttest measurements were compared using paired-samples t-tests. Results: Significant pre–post improvements were observed in estimated VO₂max, which increased from 49.82 ± 2.91 to 54.73 ± 3.08 mL·kg⁻¹·min⁻¹. Resting heart rate decreased from 72.13 ± 4.87 to 67.08 ± 4.12 beats·min⁻¹, while exercise heart rate decreased from 181.46 ± 6.35 to 174.21 ± 5.92 beats·min⁻¹. The 30-m sprint time also improved from 4.82 ± 0.31 to 4.56 ± 0.28 s. All observed differences were statistically significant (p < .001). Conclusion: A systematically structured interval-based small-sided games program was associated with improvements in aerobic fitness, heart-rate responses, and sprint performance among middle school soccer players. This approach may provide a practical and engaging conditioning strategy for school-based extracurricular soccer programs. title: IMPLEMENTATION OF PANCASILA VALUES IN THE DAILY LIVES OF PHYSICAL EDUCATION, HEALTH, AND RECREATION (PJKR) STUDENTS
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: IMPLEMENTATION OF PANCASILA VALUES IN THE DAILY LIVES OF PHYSICAL EDUCATION, HEALTH, AND RECREATION (PJKR) STUDENTS MUHAMMAD FATIR RACHMAN (289) HAMLAN KHAFIFAN NAURIL ARFAN (294) M. ZIDNY AQLI AQILA MALFARUQ (293) ABSTRACT Pancasila serves as a living philosophy for Indonesians rather than mere theoretical material memorized for examinations. For students enrolled in the Physical Education, Health, and Recreation (PJKR) program, these foundational values hold immense practical relevance across classroom lectures, athletic training, competitive matches, and everyday social interactions. This study explores how PJKR students embody Pancasila principles in their daily routines, specifically focusing on sportsmanship, discipline, tolerance, teamwork, accountability, and equity. Employing a descriptive qualitative methodology through library research, this paper examines literature sourced from academic books, scholarly journals, statutory laws, and articles covering Pancasila, character building, and physical education. The collected data were analyzed systematically via identification, categorization, interpretation, and descriptive synthesis. The findings demonstrate that all five principles of Pancasila integrate seamlessly into student life, manifested through religious tolerance, mutual respect for varying physical capacities, team cohesion, consensus-based decision-making, and equal participation in sports. Consistent practice of these ideals fosters strong personal character and equips students to become ethical physical education teachers. Ultimately, Pancasila must be actively lived in daily actions rather than passively understood in theory. Keywords: Pancasila, PJKR students, physical education, sportsmanship, character education. title: Generational change in Slovenian youth sport participation
venue: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
abstract: Background Organised sport participation during adolescence provides important physical, psychosocial, and developmental benefits, yet long-term secular trends remain insufficiently understood. This study examined decade-long changes in organised sport participation among Slovenian adolescents using nationally representative repeated cross-sectional data from the Analysis of Children's Development in Slovenia (ACDSi). Methods Data included 5,027 adolescents aged 11–18 years assessed in 2013–2014 and 2023–2024. Organised sport participation, participation history, weekly training volume, sport-category distribution, and physical fitness were analysed overall and by sex and ISCED level. Between-wave differences were tested using Pearson's chi-square tests, and training volume and fitness outcomes using general linear models. Results Organised sport participation increased from 50.4% to 63.4% ( P < .001; OR = 1.71, 95% CI 1.52–1.91), with increases observed in both sexes and both ISCED levels. In the complete-case analysis, previous participation followed by discontinuation was more common in 2023–2024 than in 2013–2014 (27.1% vs. 19.7%), although participation-history data were incomplete for a substantial proportion of 2013–2014 non-participants. Among current participants, adjusted weekly training volume increased from 4.26 to 4.99 h/week in ISCED 2 and from 4.71 to 5.30 h/week in ISCED 3. Sport-category distribution changed modestly across the decade, particularly among girls, while team sports remained the dominant category. Physical fitness differed slightly across sport categories, with the clearest differences observed for standing long-jump and 60-m sprint performance.
